newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Jan-Oct trade deficit falls five percent.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Jan-Oct trade deficit falls five percent.

text.p: Peru's trade deficit fell five percent in the first ten months of the year to $1.657 billion from $1.748 billion in the same period last year, the Central Reserve Bank said Friday.
However, the October trade gap rose 21.6 percent to $253 million from $208 million in the same month last year. MORE AC
Exports grew six percent in the first ten months to $4.840 billion from $4.583 billion in the same period of 1995, the bank said in its weekly report.
Meanwhile, in the January to October period, imports rose three percent to $6.497 billion, compared with $6.331 billion in the same period last year, the bank said.
Peru's commercial deficit more than doubled to $2.115 billion in 1995 from $1.021 billion the previous year.

The central bank report said traditional exports rose seven percent to $3.494 billion in the first ten months, while non- traditional exports were also up seven percent to $1.270 percent, and "other" exports fell 37 percent to $75 million.

Among imports, consumer goods rose six percent to $1.500 billion, raw materials were up one percent at $2.708 billion, while capital goods imports gained one percent to $1.996 billion. The bank's category of "other" goods saw imports rise 20 percent to $292 million.
